parsed.explanation: Combined national-divisive regime is high risk. Visitors face sex-binary passport/visa rules, refusal and possible lifetime ineligibility if mismatched documents create doubt about sex; facility bans in division state-run sites and criminal trespass arrests, with misgendered detention. National custody adopts conversion therapy and immigration detention reports forced labor, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse. Minors face care bans, school disclosure, sports exclusions. Absence of documented division violence is not safety; official rhetoric and state hostility reduce practical recourse. Not 0.15 because no routine arrest/imprisonment or credible execution; below 0.35 because entry refusal is linked to investigative/detention consequences and criminalized facilities. Adult with minor scores lower due mandated outing/care denial.

entry_documents.exposure: National sex-at-birth passport/visa binary, halted X markers, refusal for doubt about sex, fraud/permanent-ineligibility review; reports of confiscated or blocked passports and stranding; division follows national.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid; ongoing lawsuit, legal-aid FAQ and foreign advisories, but not operating traveler-safe passage.
entry_documents.interaction: Border mismatch can escalate to secondary screening, visa denial and possible immigration detention under fraud suspicion.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labor, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse; national corrections adopted conversion therapy, hair cuts, hormone removal and psychiatric drugs; misgendered detention risk.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Some litigation and national hate/employment law, but no documented operating traveler release protocol.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry or fraud investigation can lead to custody; treatment follows birth-sex and hostile facility rules.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars congruent access in government-funded single-sex spaces; division allows state-run bathroom restrictions; four states criminalize in some circumstances, with a reported arrest and men's-ward holding.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Use of capitol, schools, offices, prisons, hospitals or immigration facilities creates ejection, arrest and birth-sex placement paths.

care_services.exposure: Minors' gender care illegal in division; national funding and reimbursement cuts narrow access; adults may face HRT prescription refusal, though traveler incident detail is limited.
care_services.interaction: Refills, school nurse contact or emergency care may require sex-marker documents and trigger outing or denial.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive orders, visa misrepresentation, counterterrorism strategy prioritizing pro-transgender groups, local platform accusing trans people of preying, and public support for sex-document rules.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Reward memo not tied to gender identity; national employment and hate-crime coverage exist but weak locally.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Suspicion may motivate stops, refusals, custody placement and underinvestigation.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minor in guardian custody faces state-run school pronoun-disclosure, care ban, sports exclusion and private-school discrimination; guardian may be forced to out or deny care.
minors_guardians.protection: Marriage recognition and some city rules do not reach minor travel; no documented guardian-safe access.
minors_guardians.interaction: Enrollment, school emergency or clinic visit can trigger mandatory disclosure and service refusal.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No dated division trans-violence incident or rate; social hostility, party platform and absent state hate-crime coverage could worsen response.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute and local support poll; no documented visitor-protective enforcement.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: If assaulted, mismatched ID may complicate help and place a victim in birth-sex custody.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Policies contested; effective measures vary by date; unresolved birth-certificate regulation; no traveler incident data; short stay limits litigation.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Lawsuits, legal-aid FAQ, some injunctions; partial recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: A mismatch or arrest may become entry denial, custody or facility charge; remedies too slow for travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Worse than 0.25-A because of national sex-document and visa-fraud exposure, criminalized facilities, custody conversion therapy and severe immigration-abuse reports; less routine than weekly support-center raids, but more severe when detention occurs.

Similar entry exclusion and humiliating screening, but lower because refusal can link to fraud/permanent-ineligibility review, misgendered custody and state facility arrests; 0.35-A stops at denial without documented custody abuse.

Far below: 0.75-C has protective entry, trained border officers and reliable release. Here sex-binary documents, visa denial, criminal facilities and hostile custody dominate; remedies are uncertain and short-stay travelers cannot easily invoke them.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: documents and facilities are main traveler-facing triggers. A mismatched marker or sex doubt at border can refuse entry, create fraud/permanent-ineligibility review and escalate into immigration custody where reported abuse is severe. Inside the state, national and state-run facility bans plus criminal trespass allow forced ejection or arrest and birth-sex placement. Minors face care denial and mandated parental outing. Positive signals—court challenges, legal aid, existing X passports, national employment/hate-crime law—do not reliably protect a visitor and may be blocked or partial. Absence of documented street murders is not safety. The risk is high: no credible execution or routine long imprisonment, but outed travellers face coercive screening, denial, detention, care restrictions and family consequences.
